title: The Eccentric Cavity, Triple Rings, Two-armed Spirals, and Double Clumps of the MWC 758 Disk
question: What is the high-resolution sub-mm dust structure of the MWC 758 disk (cavity, rings, spirals, clumps), and what does it imply about unseen companions?

what.value: Inclination 21 deg and PA 62 deg for deprojection

evidence.loc: 3.2 The Cavity and the Outer Disk
evidence.quote: assuming an inclination $i$=21$^\circ$ and position angle PA=62$^\circ$ (cite: isella10; boehler18)

what.value: Stellar position from Gaia as phase center/origin; 160 pc

evidence.quote: located at a distance of 160$\pm$2 pc (cite: gaia18)
Combining with the total flux density of the central source measured at $\nu$=33GHz by the VLA (cite: marino15mwc758)

recipe.method: tclean Briggs 0.5 with uv taper from pipeline-calibrated data

recipe.goal: Deproject and fit inner ring ellipse
recipe.method: Deproject with i=21, PA=62 around Gaia position; fit ellipse with one focus on star, compare with offset circle
assumptions: mm dust settled to midplane so deprojection recovers face-on view

recipe.goal: Radial and azimuthal profiles of rings, arm, clumps
recipe.method: Azimuthally averaged profiles in Ring East/West; FWHM, deconvolved by sqrt(FWHM^2-beam^2); peak-to-trough contrasts
HOCHUNK3D radiative transfer models varying scale height and flaring

evidence.quote: The azimuthal peak-to-trough contrasts of the south and north clumps are 4.4 and 10
we obtain $T_{\rm dust}$=20$-$32 K at the location of the south clump

not_stated_but_needed: CLEAN threshold, niter, mask, cell and image size
Method and tools for ellipse fitting and its uncertainties
HOCHUNK3D dust/grain parameters and disk mass
score_reason: Imaging parameters mostly given and data public, but fitting and profile procedures are vague.
rediscovery_reason: Public data, stated imaging recipe, numeric feature measurements.
